findings.title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is a non-zero multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`. As a result, `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) is `false`, the next-page button remains enabled, and clicking it sets `offset` to `50` and fetches an empty page `2/2`. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((this.get("user_count") - 1) / this.get("limit")) + 1`), and `offset` in `next` / `Group#findMembers` should not be allowed to reach `user_count`.

findings.title: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing counter cache and raising on non-members
findings.body:
Replacing `group.remove(user)` with `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association causes two issues:
1. Because `:dependent` is not `:destroy` on the `has_many :through` association, ActiveRecord executes `delete_all` on `group_users` rather than destroying the `GroupUser` records, bypassing `GroupUser`'s `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` callback and leaving `groups.user_count` un-decremented.
2. Passing an integer `user_id` to `collection.delete` causes ActiveRecord to call `group.users.find(user_id)` first, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the user is already not a member of the group.

findings.title: add_members raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique when adding an existing member
findings.body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each username without checking whether the user is already in `group.users`. Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)` and the admin UI neither filters out existing members nor clears the `user-selector` input after adding, attempting to add a user who is already in the group raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (HTTP 500).

findings.title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
findings.body: The admin group template displays the `alias_level` selector when creating a new group and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` includes `alias_level` in the `POST /admin/groups` payload, but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and ignores `params[:alias_level]` (unlike `update`, which sets `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`). Any alias level selected during group creation is silently lost.

findings.title: Public group members page only displays the first 50 members with no way to view the rest
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now paginate with a default `limit` of 50, but the public group members template (`group/members.hbs`) and route (`group-members.js.es6`) have no pagination or load-more mechanism. Any group with more than 50 members will only ever show the first 50 members on `/groups/:name/members`.
